summary: Gregory Price Grieve works in religious studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his BA at San Francisco State University and master's and doctoral degrees at the University of Chicago, later becoming Professor and Head of Religious Studies at UNC Greensboro.

Gregory Schopen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Black Hills State, McMaster, and the Australian National University under Jan Willem de Jong and Tissa Rajapatirana. He held professorships at UT Austin and UCLA.

Grigory Maksimovich Bongard-Levin specialized in Indology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at the MSU Institute of Asian and African Studies under George de Roerich, he held posts at the Institute of Oriental Studies and Moscow State University.
Gritli von Mitterwallner was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist. She earned her Dr. phil. and Habilitation at the University of Munich, where she later served as Professor from 1978 to 1991.

Gu Jiegang worked in history, archaeology, and Sinology. After studying at Peking University under Shih Hu and Taiyan Zhang, he taught there and at Fudan University, later holding posts at the Chinese Academy of Sciences and CASS.
Gu Rong Gyalsé Chökyi Lodrö studied under Shechen Gyaltsab and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.

Guang Xing is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his PhD at SOAS and the University of London under Tadeusz Skorupski and Timothy Hugh Barrett. He held posts at the University of Hong Kong and the University of British Columbia.

Guangchang Fang specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He served as a researcher at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences from circa 1986 to 2000 and became a professor at Shanghai Normal University around 2000.
Guankong worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He served as a teacher at the Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Institute and as a professor at the Buddhist Academy of China beginning in 1957.

Gudrun Bühnemann is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Bonn under Michael Hahn and at Vienna under Ernst Steinkellner. She held fellowships in India and Japan before joining the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1992.
Gudrun Melzer is a scholar of Indology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She completed her doctoral studies at the University of Munich under the supervision of Jens-Uwe Hartmann.

Gudō Wafu Nishijima was a Buddhist studies practitioner and scholar who studied law at the University of Tokyo and trained under Kodo Sawaki and Renpō Niwa. He lectured at the University of Tokyo and the Eastern Institute.
Gunapala Dharmasiri is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who held posts at the University of Peradeniya, attested in 1991 and 2008.

Gunapala Piyasena Malalasekera was an Indologist and Buddhist studies linguist. Educated at the University of London and SOAS under Caroline Rhys Davids and William Stede, he became Dean of Oriental Studies at the University of Ceylon.
Gunilla Gren-Eklund is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Stig Wikander. She held a post at Uppsala University from circa 1974 to 2003.
Gunnar Jarring was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Lund University from 1926 to 1933 and held a post there from 1933 to 1940.

Guo Jun is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who studied at Fuyan Buddhist Institute, Monash University, and the University of Sydney, training under Sheng Yen, Song Nian, and Qinyin. He served as abbot at Mahabodhi Monastery.
Guohui Shi is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Rissho University under Kenyu Mitomo and studied under Sheng Yen alongside several other teachers.

Gurinder Singh Mann is a religious studies and Indology scholar. Educated at Baring Union Christian College, Kent, Harvard, and Columbia, he taught religion at Columbia University and held the Kapany Chair in Sikh Studies at UC Santa Barbara.

id: P:Gustaaf Adolf van den Bergh van Eysinga
summary: Gustaaf Adolf van den Bergh van Eysinga was a religious studies scholar. He studied at Leiden University from circa 1893 to 1901 and later held posts at Utrecht University and the University of Amsterdam.
